sources.title: EAC Partner States
sources.officialityEvidence: The EAC Secretariat's live official page identifies Burundi, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, and Tanzania as current EAC Partner States.
sources.supportingExcerpt: The EAC comprises eight (8) Partner States ... Democratic Republic of the Congo ... Republic of Burundi ... United Republic of Tanzania.

sources.title: Visa-Free Entry
sources.officialityEvidence: The EAC Secretariat's current Immigration and Labour guidance says every Partner State implements Article 7(1) visa-free entry for citizens of other Partner States.
sources.supportingExcerpt: All Partner States are implementing Article 7(1) ... provision for visa-free entry of citizens of EAC Partner States.

sources.title: Suspension of visa issuance to foreign nationals
sources.officialityEvidence: The current State Department notice implements Presidential Proclamation 10998, effective 1 January 2026, and expressly includes Burundi in the partial suspension.
sources.supportingExcerpt: The Department of State partially suspended visa issuance ... Burundi.

sources.title: 8 U.S.C. 1101: Definitions
sources.publisher: Office of the Law Revision Counsel, U.S. House of Representatives
sources.officialityEvidence: The official current U.S. Code compilation defines the INA's geographical United States to include Puerto Rico, Guam, the U.S. Virgin Islands, and CNMI.
sources.supportingExcerpt: means the continental United States, Alaska, Hawaii, Puerto Rico, Guam, the Virgin Islands ... and the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands

policies.title: Burundian ordinary passports: EAC visa-free short visits
policies.summary: Current EAC immigration guidance establishes visa-free entry for citizens of one Partner State into another; Burundi, the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Tanzania are current Partner States.
conditions: Applies to an ordinary Burundian passport holder travelling for a short visitor stay under the EAC Partner-State visa-free entry rule.
Work, residence, study, special passes, diplomatic or official documents, border operations, carrier requirements and final admission remain outside this classification.
